Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Vivek Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
Heard Mr. Vivek Tripathi, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant Shivakant Rathaur @ Nitin seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.171 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 (2) IPC and Sections 3/4 Pocso Act, police station Shivrajpur, district Kanpur Nagar, during the pendency of trial.
Perused the record.

sentences.text: 1 At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. submits that notice of present application for bail has been served upon the first informant-opposite party-2 on 13.06.2023.
However, in spite of service of notice, no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant-opposite party-2 to oppose the application for bail.
At the very outset, the learned counsel for applicant has invited the attention of the Court to the order dated 17.07.2023 passed in present application.
For ready reference, the same is reproduced herein-under :-
"Heard Sri Vivek Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

By means of the present bail application, the applicant is involved in case crime no.
171 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376(2) IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S.
Shivrajpur, District Kanpur Nagar.

Submission made by the counsel that as per the FIR the age of the girl is 17 years as per her school leaving certificate of class V. There is nothing on record to establish the age of the victim on the date of the incident.
Under such circumstances, CMM, Kanpur Nagar and CMO, Kanpur Nagar are directed to organize the ossification test of the victim.

CMO, Kanpur Nagar is required to constitute a panel of three senior doctors, who shall conduct the ossification test of the victim and give opinion about the expected age of the victim on the date of the incident to be disclosed by the victim or the informant of the case.

This exercise has to be completed within a period of 15 days and CMM, Kanpur Mainpuri shall ensure the presence of victim before the panel of doctor and give its report in a sealed cover on or before 09.08.2023 before this Court.
Put up this case as fresh on 08.08.2023 before appropriate Court.
Let copy of this order may be given to learned AGA for communication and compliance of the order."
Pursuant to above order dated 17.07.2023, the Chief Medical Officer, Kanpur Dehat constituted a Medical Board to determine the medical age of the prosecutrix.
Accordingly, the Board has submitted it's report dated 04.08.2023 to this Court in a sealed envelop as per which the prosecutrix is aged about 18 years.

Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 14.09.2022, a delayed F.I.R. dated 15.09.2022 was lodged by first informant, namely, Sarvesh Kashyap (father of Shivakant Rathaur @ Nitin vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197523487/
2 the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No.0171 of 2022, under Section 363 IPC, police station Shivrajpur, district Kanpur (Outer).

sentences.text: In the aforesaid F.I.R., an un-known person has been arraigned as a solitary accused.
The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. dated 15.09.2022 is to the effect that the daughter of first informant i.e. prosecutrix, namely, X aged about 17 years has gone missing.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that applicant is innocent.
He is not named in the FIR.
However, though the applicant is a charge-sheeted accused inasmuch as the charge-sheet has been submitted against applicant on 16.10.2022 yet the applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC, which is on record at page 32 of the paper book, has not alleged that her modesty was dislodged by the applicant.
In short, the prosecutrix has not supported the FIR.
Thereafter, the prosecutrix was requested for medical examination but the same was refused by her.
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 CrPC, which is on record at page 38 of the paper book, wherein she has alleged that applicant has dislodged her modesty.
On the above premise, the learned counsel for applicant contends that the prosecutrix in her statements recorded under Sections 161/164 CrPC has not remained clear, categorical and consistent.
The allegation of rape by the applicant has been made for the first time in the statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 CrPC.
The contradiction, exaggeration, embellishment that has emerged in the subsequent statement of the prosecutrix
, as noted above, has not been explained by the prosecutrix herself.

There is no medical evidence to support the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 CrPC, inasmuch as,
the prosecutrix herself refused for her internal medical examination.

Referring to the judgement of the Supreme Court in Phool Singh Vs.State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74, he contends that conviction of an accused for an offence of rape and sexual assault can be maintained in the absence of medical evidence and on the solitary statement of the prosecutrix.

entities.text: Phool Singh Vs.State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in such a circumstance the statement of the prosecutrix should be clear, categorical and consistent.

When the aforesaid test is applied to the facts of the present case and the statements of the prosecutrix referred to above are examined as a whole they do not fall in the category of impeccable evidence.
He therefore submits that no prosecution of the applicant can be maintained on the basis of above.

Even otherwise,
applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
The applicant is in jail since 29.09.2022.
As such he has undergone more than ten months of incarceration.
The police report under Section 173(2) CrPC has already been submitted.
As such the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized.
Up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of the applicant.
He therefore submits that the applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that though the applicant is not named in the FIR but a charge-sheeted accused therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence of this Court.
The applicant is guilty of dislodging of modesty of the prosecutrix who was a young girl aged about 17 years at the time of occurrence.

The complicity of the applicant in the crime in question is clearly established as per the statement of the prosecurix recorded under Section 164 Shivakant Rathaur @ Nitin vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197523487/
3

sentences.text: CrPC therefore, no sympathy be shown by this court in favour of the applicant.
However, he could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for the applicant with reference to the record at this stage.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence, complicity of the accused, accusation made, nature and gravity of offence and coupled with the fact that the statements of the prosecutrix as recorded under Section 161/164 CrPC are inconsistent and contradictory, the embellishment emerging in the statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 CrPC having not been explained, the judgement of the Supreme Court in Phool Singh (supra), referred to above, wherein it has been categorically held that prosecution of an accused for an offence of rape/sexual assault can be maintained even in the absence of medical evidence and on the basis of the solitary statement of the prosecutrix, however,
in such a situation the statements of the prosecutrix referred to above when taken as a whole do not fall in the category of incapable character, even though the charge-sheet having been submitted therefore the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized, but inspite of above no such circumstance could be pointed out by the learned A.G.A.
necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant, Sumit Subhashchandra Gangwal Vs. State of Maharashtra 2023 Live Law (SC) 373 (paragraph 5), the clean antecedents of the applicant, the period of incarceration undergone, but without making any comment on the merits of the case, the applicant has made out a case for bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant Shivakant Rathaur @ Nitin, involved in aforesaid case crime number, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under section 229-A I.P.C.
(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under section 174-A I.P.C.
Shivakant Rathaur @ Nitin vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197523487/
4

entities.text: Shivakant Rathaur @ Nitin vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial within a period of one year after the release of the applicant.

However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his bail so granted by this court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
